answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of escrowed trades with distinct counterparties; each counterparty must lock funds and later confirm delivery, while disputes slash the bond. A new identity therefore cannot gain influence merely by appearing: it must finance real exchanges across a long horizon and risk losing stake to dishonest partners. Splitting capital among cedar- or shale-named accounts does not multiply that capital, so a sybil attacker pays in locked funds, fees, and exposure for every credible identity.
